description.value: This preliminary study examined the extent to which regional brain activation during a reward cue antisaccade (AS) task was associated with 6-month treatment outcome in adolescent substance users.

spans.text: This preliminary study examined the extent to which regional brain activation during a reward cue antisaccade (AS) task was associated with 6-month treatment outcome in adolescent substance users.

value: We hypothesized that when preparing to execute an AS, greater activation in regions associated with cognitive (e.g., dlPFC, vlPFC) and oculomotor (e.g., FEF, SEF) control which support AS would be associated with lower severity of substance involvement at 6-month follow-up.

We also predicted that the association between regional activation and treatment outcome would be stronger for reward, relative to neutral, trials because reward cues may motivate and optimize effective cognitive control in adolescents.

spans.text: In addition, we hypothesized that when preparing to execute an AS (preparation phase), greater activation in regions involved in cognitive (  e.g.  , dlPFC, vlPFC) and oculomotor (  e.g.  , FEF, SEF) control which support AS would be associated with lower severity of substance involvement at 6-month follow-up.

description.value: A longitudinal, naturalistic study of youth recruited from community-based intensive outpatient treatment for substance use, with baseline, 6-month, and 1-year follow-up assessments and fMRI scanning during or shortly after treatment completion.

definition.value: Activation in reward-condition ROIs was inversely correlated with marijuana symptom count at 6-month follow-up.

spans.text: Note: N = 14.

value: In the reward condition, activation in regions associated with reward (amygdala, nAcc), executive functioning (left vlPFC sphere), and oculomotor control (SEF sphere, putamen) were inversely correlated with marijuana symptoms at 6-months.

Those with fewer symptoms at 6-months tended to show greater activation in the ROI relative to baseline fixation, whereas those with more symptoms at follow-up tended to show deactivation in the ROI relative to baseline fixation.

spans.text: Likewise, when contrasting activation in reward   versus   neutral conditions, greater activation during reward   versus   neutral condition in ROIs associated with reward (left amygdala, left nAcc), executive function (right vlPFC sphere), and oculomotor control (putamen) were inversely correlated with 6-month marijuana symptom count, controlling for the covariates.

spans.text: fMRI reward cue antisaccade (AS) task

description.value: Fast-event-related reward-cue antisaccade task with reward and neutral trials and separately modeled cue, preparation, and response epochs.

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to look at the mirror location of the peripheral target, perform the antisaccade, and try to obtain the maximum reward.

stimuli.value: Green dollar-sign or blue pound-sign cue rings, a red fixation cross, and a peripheral yellow target dot.
